body:
### Problem

First reported at nvim-mini/mini.nvim#2562. vim.pack behaves slightly differently but has the same shape of bug.

### What goes wrong?

vim.pack passes the ambient environment to git and unsets only `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/521eddec7c243a8166609bf1734cb940e9510fc5/runtime/lua/vim/pack.lua#L307-L312

`GIT_INDEX_FILE` survives. Installs clone with `--no-checkout` and populate the worktree with a separate `git checkout`, which then reads that index instead of the plugin's own. The checkout fails, but git exits 0, so vim.pack reports success and leaves the plugin directory containing only .git. It never recovers: later startups see the directory and treat the plugin as installed.

git's stderr reaches vim.notify, but vim.pack writes its "100%" progress line after it, so nothing is visible interactively. It only appears in `:messages`.
The failed checkout also sends the unrelated repo's blob hashes to the plugin's remote.

### When does this happen?

git sets always `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (to ./git/index) for `$EDITOR` but this is only a problem when git is ran with `--git-dir`, which makes the index file path absolute. So this is not a particularly obscure thing, it will happen whenever interactively editing a commit or interactively rebasing with `--git-dir` specified. I encountered it because I [manage my dotfiles in a bare git repo](https://www.atlassian.com/git/tutorials/dotfiles) which involves running a lot of `git --git-dir`.

Not reproduced on nightly, but the code is identical on master.

### Steps to reproduce

Any repo works as the index source:

    mkdir /tmp/bug && cd /tmp/bug
    git init -q .
    echo hi > file.txt
    git add file.txt
    git commit -m "add file.txt"

Add the following to minimal.lua. Make sure after you create this you _don't_ let vim.pack install:

    vim.pack.add({ 'https://github.com/gpanders/nvim-parinfer' })

Run:

    GIT_EDITOR='nvim --clean -u /tmp/bug/minimal.lua' git --git-dir=/tmp/bug/.git commit --amend

Answer the install prompt with y, then `:messages`:

    vim.pack: Installing plugins (0/1)
    fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref 45b983be36b73c0788dc9cbcb76cbb80fc7bb057
    error: invalid object 100644 45b983be36b73c0788dc9cbcb76cbb80fc7bb057 for 'file.txt'
    vim.pack: 100% Installing plugins (1/1)

`45b983be` is file.txt from /tmp/bug, requested from gpanders/nvim-parinfer.

Nothing was checked out:

    $ ls -a ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/nvim-parinfer
    .  ..  .git

Restarting nvim does not fix it.

### Expected behavior

The plugin installs correctly. Git state from the ambient environment should not reach vim.pack's git calls. You might be interested in how [pre-commit solves this][]:

```python
def no_git_env(_env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    # Too many bugs dealing with environment variables and GIT:
    # https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit/issues/300
    # In git 2.6.3 (maybe others), git exports GIT_WORK_TREE while running
    # pre-commit hooks
    # In git 1.9.1 (maybe others), git exports GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE
    # while running pre-commit hooks in submodules.
    # GIT_DIR: Causes git clone to clone wrong thing
    # GIT_INDEX_FILE: Causes 'error invalid object ...' during commit
    _env = _env if _env is not None else os.environ
    return {
        k: v for k, v in _env.items()
        if not k.startswith('GIT_') or
        k.startswith(('GIT_CONFIG_KEY_', 'GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_')) or
        k in {
            'GIT_EXEC_PATH', 'GIT_SSH', 'GIT_SSH_COMMAND', 'GIT_SSL_CAINFO',
            'GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY', 'GIT_CONFIG_COUNT',
            'GIT_HTTP_PROXY_AUTHMETHOD',
            'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL',
            'GIT_ASKPASS',
        }
    }
```

[pre-commit solves this]: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit/blob/a9bba55a3f74068b53f4bd4d831d7e05e34eae6c/pre_commit/git.py#L27-L48

Separately, `git checkout` exiting 0 after printing "error: invalid object" probably should not count as a successful install but that's kinda git's problem

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.5 (LuaJIT 2.1.1788856981)

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

no, it doesn't include vim.pack

### Operating system/version

Fedora Linux 44

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.47.1

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-kitty

### Installation

Homebrew

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> Answer the install prompt with y, then `:messages`:

That's the part that I'd argue against. There is an opportunity to discard installing a plugin in a (clearly) not the best situation for it.

And pressing `n` seems to cleanly not attempt an install while the current usage as `GIT_EDITOR` seems to continue working cleanly.

However, if #42114 is all it takes to fix this, then maybe it is worth doing. Not particularly eager going down the route of `pre-commit` example mentioned here.

title: vim.pack: inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE makes plugin install silently fail
